newsitem.title: USA: Henkel, Loctite agree to merge.
newsitem.headline: Henkel, Loctite agree to merge.

text.p: Henkel KGaA and Loctite Corp said Thursday they reached a friendly merger whereby Henkel would acquire the 65 percent of Loctite it does not currently own for $61 per share cash.
The agreement, unanimously approved by Loctite's board, comes five weeks of after Henkel first unveiled a proposal to buy Loctite for $56 per share.
Late yesterday, Henkel raised its bid to the agreed-to price, and conditioned the transaction on a deal acceptable to both parties.

"Henkel's increased offer represents excellent value for our shareholders. The proposal comes at the end of a process designed to produce the best transaction," said Robert Fiondella, chairman of the Loctite special board committee set up to weigh offers for the Hartford-based adhesives and specialty chemical company.

Dieter Winkhaus, chief executive of Dusseldorf-based Henkel, said, "We see a continuing role of importance for the management and employees of Loctite in the ongoing, combined business. Moreover, we expect the Hartford office to remain an important center for the operation of our combined adhesives business going forward."
Winkhaus was alluding to Henkel's conforming with Loctite's bid condition that the Hartford office remain open for at least two years.

In Henkel's filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on its increased offer, made last night, Winkhaus said in a letter to the special Loctite committee, "We have accepted the language proposed in your draft agreement requiring that the corporate headquarters be maintained in Hartford for two years. We anticipate that the office will be maintained for an even longer period."
In morning New York Stock Exchange trade, Loctite shares were up 3/8 to 60-3/4.
